scope: 5 reversed protosegments (segmentids 0016558, 0343093-0343096)
description: Prod doesn't reverse these protosegments: two or more reversed protosegments touch one segment, and prod's sequential updates flip its fields back and forth until they cancel out. Ours reverses them.

scope: 10 non-street segments inside Randall's Island, left and right zip
description: Prod leaves both zip codes blank; ours fills 10035, the only zip on the island, from the spatial fallback.

scope: Curve flag on compound-curve shoreline, subway and rail segments
description: Ours flags these curves irregular (I) where prod is blank: prod's irregular-curve test doesn't work on compound curves.

scope: BOE LGC pointer on segments with two-digit LGC codes
description: Prod's pointer is its default 1 where ours points at the right LGC: prod mis-parses two-digit LGC codes. 567 LION records on 26c; the two older write-ups (568 records on 5 face codes; 67 Queens records) were never reconciled.

scope: Segment sequence number on non-street features
description: Sequence numbers for non-street features are generated each build and don't match prod's. They only need to be unique within LION.

scope: Coincident segment count, segment 8101066 (Brooklyn)
description: A centerline and two rail/subway segments meet at one point; ours counted 3, prod 2, because our count merged subway and rail into one feature type. Fixed: no longer differs on 26c.

scope: ArcCenterX, ArcCenterY and Radius
description: Implemented as prod does: 0 on non-curved segments, radius measured from the rounded center. 9,801 of 9,802 curved segments match; the last is within rounding.

scope: VIntersect on the node layer
description: Was hardcoded null. Now follows the legacy rule (a listed virtual intersection with at least one intersecting street segment); row counts and value distribution match prod.

scope: altnames: Join_IDs only one side's LION carries
description: Fixed: node street-name abbreviation, and a SAF Join_ID now lists its host segment's names, as prod does (66,056 diff rows down to 12). The remaining altnames rows belong to Join_IDs that only one side's LION has.

scope: lion layer row key, LegacyID and Join_ID padding
description: The LegacyID mismatch came from comparing on a key that isn't unique; the comparison now keys on SegmentID and Join_ID. Prod's lion-layer Join_ID lacks the trailing padding the spec requires (prod's own altnames layer has it): ours keeps the padding and the comparison allows for it.

scope: Segment locational status, X case
description: Uses 2010 census tracts, as prod does, where 2020 tracts would be right. Matched on purpose (issue #2193).

scope: Segment 133963 traffic direction; segment 241972 special address flag
description: Two diffs GR/GSS flagged: 133963 was A in ours, W in prod; 241972 is N in ours, blank in prod. On 26c, 133963 no longer differs and 241972 is accounted for by the hand review (CSCL-LION-17). No answer from GR/GSS yet.

scope: Street on the lion layer
description: Was hardcoded null. Now the segment's principal street name, by the same rule as altnames; null rate and distinct values match prod closely.

scope: Coincident segment count, segment 359093 (Bronx)
description: Prod's BronxLION.dat has 0, which the spec forbids; ours is 1, the spec's value for no coincident segments.

scope: House-number fields on generic segments
description: The spec zeroes all eight house-number fields on generic segments, and ours does; prod has real values on 42% of them (5,743 of 13,592). The legacy rule is a manually run cleanup tool, which likely misses segments changed since it last ran.

scope: Left/right AtomicPolygon and the fields derived from it, on about 100 segments
description: Ours takes a segment's side AtomicPolygons from the AtomicPolygon edges it runs along; prod's 2 ft probe overshoots into the polygon behind where the adjacent one is shallow (corners, slivers). Census, district and locational-status fields differ on those segments.

scope: 12 LION records reviewed one by one
description: Each record was checked by hand against source (Aug 2026): ours is right. 11 still differ on 26c. The SAF S record reviewed with them (416070284412) was withdrawn: source says LGC 01, as prod has.

scope: Segment 358043 (Staten Island), every left/right district and census field
description: Our curve loader read a zero-length arc as a full circle, so the segment's side points fell far outside the city and every side field came out blank. Fixed in the FGDB reader (#2778).

scope: Special address flag on ramp protosegment, segment 174704 (Queens)
description: Prod prints B on an R-type ramp protosegment, carried over from its centerline record; the legacy rule says ramps never carry the flag. Ours is blank.

scope: SAF rows on the lion layer, SpecAddr types A, B, E and P
description: Ours adds one row per SAF record on a segment, as prod does, but writes fewer A, B, E and P rows than prod (241,999 rows vs 243,706): prod repeats some records per parity, which isn't implemented.

scope: From/to node of roadbed segment, segment 133963
description: Ours picked a segment's rows in no fixed order and could take the reversed protosegment's nodes. Fixed by taking the centerline row first; 23 other segments with conflicting node pairs weren't re-checked.

scope: Polygon part counts on nymcea and nynta2020
description: GDAL misread polygons with many rings on export; fixed for nypuma2010 and nypuma2020 by dropping holes below the minimum area. Fragmentation on nymcea, and the clip-fragmentation gap on nynta2020, are separate and unexplained.

scope: Area on nyhez, nycdwi and nypp, under 0.5%
description: nyhez and nycdwi have invalid source polygons that GEOS repairs differently from prod's ArcGIS. nypp's source is valid, so its +0.34% is something else, not yet found.

scope: SHAPE_Length on coastline rows of layers clipped to the shoreline
description: Gaps in AtomicPolygon coverage at the shoreline and at jurisdictional edges inflate the clipped outline. Fixed for nynta2010 and nynta2020; the other shoreline-clipped layers still show it.

scope: nybid, BID 56 (South Shore)
description: Source BID 56 is invalid: one ring sits inside another. Prod publishes it as is, with a SHAPE_Area that treats the inner ring as a hole; ours publishes it made valid, so geometry and SHAPE_Area agree.

scope: nybid, nycdwi, nyhd, nymcea, nyura and nyzip
description: FileGDB metadata shows these six prod layers haven't been regenerated since October 2009, so they don't follow current source. (The same evidence on the LION altnames layer no longer explains its diffs: see CSCL-LION-09.)

scope: Transitory elimination, about 3% of records
description: A segment created and retired between releases should be dropped with its whole lineage. The legacy rule's source isn't available; ours approximates it (97.4% recall, 96.1% precision on two editions).

scope: L and R journal record types
description: CENTERLINEHISTORY has L and R records that no published edition contains; their counts mirror G and P. Ours drops them.

scope: Cumulative record number
description: Record numbers should run on across editions; prod's own sequence has a hand-entry gap (25B to 25C). Ours continues from the previous edition's header, so it drifts if prod's does.

scope: One LION record with GENERICID -1
description: Bad source data: one record citywide (26b) has GENERICID -1, which reaches the file as 00000-1. Ours guards its casts so the build doesn't fail.

scope: Type S LGCs and ABCEGNPX row counts
description: Once filed as stale prod data; all were ours. Type S: a point whose street isn't on its segment's LGC list takes LGC1 from its own street (LGC2-4 blank), LGC2-4 follow the segment's LGC row order, and an S record reaching the generic file through the RPL takes the generic segment's name. ABCEGNPX: first RPL row per roadbed, the protosegment for RPL rows, and no record for an unnamed CommonPlace.

scope: ABCEGNPX G/N/X side AtomicPolygon, borough and census tract, about 65 rows per file
description: These CommonPlace points sit on an AtomicPolygon boundary (all within 0.0002 ft), where GEOS and Esri disagree on which polygon contains them.

scope: ABCEGNPX, segment 9017010
description: Prod includes an AltSegmentData row with a blank ALT_SEGDATA_TYPE, as the legacy code does; ours leaves it out, following spec Table 13.

scope: ABCEGNPX, 2 duplicate-key groups per file
description: Ours writes two rows where prod writes one: a CommonPlace point inside two overlapping AtomicPolygons, and a street code with two principal names in source. The keyed comparison can't see these.

scope: SND, Enders and Exception rows only one side has
description: Prod was built from a newer CSCL extract than ours (inferred from code sequencing; no newer extract to check against). Once filed as stale prod entries.

scope: Congressional, state senate, municipal court and city council district
description: About 2% of rows differed on fields for offices redistricted since the last cycle; against GR's corrected 26c thined.txt, nothing differs.

scope: File header
description: Prod's thined.txt starts with a 3-line header; ours now writes it. The record count is computed; the other two lines' meaning is unconfirmed, so they come from config.

scope: nyc.thinlion trailing end-of-file marker
description: Prod's file ends with a DOS end-of-file byte, which the comparison read as an extra row. Comparison fix, not an output difference.

scope: Police precinct, sector and patrol borough on 7 sliver AtomicPolygons
description: These AtomicPolygons straddle a precinct boundary, and GEOS's centroid lands on the other side of it from Esri's.

scope: Bronx patrol borough
description: Prod has the split Bronx patrol boroughs (XN, XS) where ours had BX, from our source's patrol borough layer. No rows differ on 26c.

scope: Borough of 12 fire companies
description: Ours picked whichever AtomicPolygon carried the company code first, putting 12 companies in the wrong borough's file. Now a point-in-polygon match on the company's centroid.
